audience: GitHub Copilot is for developers who already have an editor and want completions and some agent usage without a research project. The verdict says it is the best value for most developers, and that $10 gets you solid completions and agent usage inside the editor you already use. VS Code, JetBrains, and the CLI are the places it runs.

It is a weaker fit if you wanted the deepest agent and you are willing to babysit a disputed price page. The cons say it has less agentic depth than Cursor. If the job is a long multi-file agent session, read Claude Code too. If the job is everyday completion, start here.
features: The ladder is simple, which is rare in this category. Free is $0 and includes 2,000 completions a month. Pro is $10 a month. Pro+ is $39 a month. Max is $100 a month. Business is $19 per user a month. Those are the rows in the billing docs we checked on 14 October 2026.

A generous free tier is a real pro. Two thousand completions is enough to learn whether the suggestions match your codebase. It is not a promise about agent credits. The cons say the usage-credit model is complex, and this page does not reprint a credit formula the billing doc's plan rows do not state.

Cheap entry is the point of the verdict. Pro at $10 undercuts Claude Pro at $20 and the Cursor docs price of $20. You are paying less, and you should expect the agent to be less deep. That trade is the review.
limitations: The usage-credit model is complex. We will not invent a translation from completions to agent tasks. If your team needs a hard cap written in tasks, this plan list does not give you one.
Less agentic depth than Cursor is a product limit, not a pricing complaint. Cursor's own price list is in dispute, so the deeper agent is not automatically the better buy. It is a different risk.
Business at $19 per user is the team door in the table. We do not have a separate enterprise dollar amount, so we do not add one. The Worth it verdict is about the individual Pro seat at $10.
pricingNotes: From the GitHub Copilot billing docs, checked 14 October 2026. Free is $0 for 2,000 completions a month. Pro is $10 a month. Pro+ is $39 a month. Max is $100 a month. Business is $19 per user a month.

There is no pricing note on the tool beyond those rows, and no annual price in the table, so none is printed. The usage-credit model is called complex in the cons and is not expanded into a rate card here.

faqs.a: For most developers, that is the verdict. Pro is $10 a month for completions and agent usage in the editor you already use. Pro+ at $39 and Max at $100 are there if the credit model runs out, not as the default.

faqs.q: What does the free plan include?
faqs.a: Free is $0 and includes 2,000 completions a month. It is a real trial of the suggestions. It is not described here as an agent allowance, because the row does not say that.
The cons say the model is complex. We do not publish a conversion that is not in the plan rows. Read the billing docs before you assume completions and agent tasks draw the same meter.

faqs.q: Is there an affiliate link on this verdict?
faqs.a: No. There is no affiliate relationship in the data. The Worth it rating is the $10 value, not a commission.
